$comment: Hand-written assertions of the product's placement rule: a compound is placed by INTENDED EFFECT, never by signalling pathway, and never on the organ that merely clears or metabolises it. The build enforces every rule below and fails on a violation. Add a rule when a placement decision was hard enough to be worth freezing; do not add one that merely restates the schema.

rules.reason: GH secretagogues, GHRH analogues and growth hormone itself are placed on the pituitary — the site of the intended effect — not on liver (where IGF-1 is made) or muscle (where the downstream effect lands).
rules.$note: Deliberately matches the GH-AXIS agents only. AOD-9604 is a growth hormone C-terminal fragment with no somatotroph activity, so a bare `growth hormone` match would wrongly demand a pituitary placement for it.

when.class_matches: GHRH|ghrelin receptor|recombinant human growth hormone|growth hormone derivative

rules.reason: GLP-1, GIP and amylin agonists are placed on the pancreas. Weight change is a downstream consequence and belongs on `body` as burdens, not as a second acts_on.

Androgens, androgen esters and anabolic-androgenic steroids are placed on the gonads. Erythrocytosis, prostatic growth and lipid shift are burdens, not intended effects — except where an approved label states otherwise, which is why `blood` is not forbidden here.
rules.$note: The lookbehind excludes ANTIandrogens (spironolactone, the 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors), which are not placed on the gonads by this rule.

rules.reason: The liver is where HMG-CoA reductase sits, but lowering cardiovascular risk is the intended effect. Statins are placed on the heart; the liver is burdens.
SERMs and aromatase inhibitors are placed on the gonads — the sex-steroid axis they modulate — not on the pituitary that transmits the feedback change.
Thyroid hormones and antithyroid agents are placed on the thyroid. Cardiac and skeletal effects of over- or under-replacement are burdens.
An organ a compound is merely cleared by, excreted through, or metabolised in is burdens or confounds — never acts_on. This is the rule most easily broken by accident.
A toxicity, injury or adverse-effect claim is never an intended effect. If the note describes harm, the relation must be burdens or confounds.
`confounds` means the compound distorts a MEASUREMENT without acting on the system. If the note does not talk about a reading, value, marker or assay, the relation is probably burdens.
